chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad from Hariz from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Bukayr from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the zakat: for what is irrigated with effort (using tools like buckets and pulleys), there is half the tithe (2.5%); and if it is irrigated without effort, from a river, or a spring, or by rain (natural rainfall), then there is the full tithe (5%).

key_terms.الدِّلَاء: Irrigation using pulleys or ropes to lift water
key_terms.الرِّشَاء: Irrigation using buckets or simple tools requiring effort
key_terms.النَّوَاضِح: Irrigation using beasts of burden to carry water

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in zakat rates for crops irrigated by effort versus natural sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the principle of equity in zakat by linking the tax burden to the cost of cultivation, distinguishing between labor-intensive irrigation (yielding 2.5%) and natural irrigation (yielding 5%). This distinction reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness, ensuring that those who incur greater effort in maintaining their crops are not overburdened compared to those benefiting from natural water sources. It serves as a foundational text for the calculation of 'ushr in agricultural jurisprudence.
